details:
DR. ASHOK KUMAR
MITTAL (Punjab):
Sir, the Order of Precedence in India is a protocol list in which the
Government of Indias functionaries and authorities are listed by rank and
office. It is designed for State and ceremonial events. It has no application
in the Governments day-to-day operations. The President of India issues the
Order which is maintained by the Ministry of Home Affairs. Currently, the
Members of Parliament are listed at number 21 in the Table of Precedence which
is even below the statutory posts like Cabinet Secretary, Chairman, Central
Administrative Tribunal and Chairman, Minorities Commission. A Member of
Parliament is elected through the mechanism laid down in the Constitution of
India. A Member of Parliament represents the will of the people and is their
voice in the Parliament, and in addition to this, he is also entrusted with
representing his State and also the country at multiple forums. However, the
low ranking in the table of precedence doesnt do justice to the stature and
sanctity of a Member of Parliament which needs to be changed in a
representative democracy like India, which takes pride in its parliamentary
system of governance where its citizens decide their representatives, including
the Prime Minister, the President and the Vice-President. I request the
Government that in view of the important constitutional, statutory and
legislative functions being discharged by the Members of Parliament and Members
of Legislative Assembly, the table of precedence should be revised and entry
15, which is accorded to Cabinet Ministers in State Government, should be given
to the Members of Parliament and Members of Legislative Assembly who reflect
the aspirations of their electorate as policy makers.
(Ends)
